key_insight: LLM-generated note bloat modestly degraded downstream summaries, while unconfirmed diagnoses propagated into later LLM outputs without detectable changes in standard quality metrics.
clinical_relevance: AI-authored medical records may influence subsequent AI documentation, making content provenance and diagnostic uncertainty important to monitor.
method: Evaluated seven reader models from four families.
Compared accumulated LLM summaries with length-matched copy-forward and templated text.
Injected unconfirmed differential diagnoses and tested their reappearance in downstream outputs.
evidence_signal: Across the tested models, LLM summaries modestly but consistently reduced hospital-course generation quality, and diagnostic-overcall propagation varied by reader model.
watch_item: Standard quality metrics did not detect changes associated with overcall propagation, suggesting a need for targeted evaluation of diagnostic uncertainty.
paper_title: AI in the Clinical Documentation Loop: Effects of LLM-Induced Note Bloat and Diagnostic Overcall on Downstream LLMs
